name: agent-definition-runtime-loop
explain: Demonstrates defining an agent with instructions, model adapter, tool registry, and execution limits. Shows how a dynamic agent loop inspects intermediate observations to select subsequent tools and differentiates an autonomous agent from a fixed pipeline, enforcing hard ceilings on turns, tokens, and loop detection.
steps: Instantiate an agent configuration specifying instructions, model, tools, and execution bounds. || Execute an autonomous task where the agent dynamically chooses actions based on runtime feedback. || Enforce hard bounding policies including turn limits, token ceilings, and duplicate action detection.
expect: Agent definition, dynamic runtime loop, and execution bounding verified successfully.

name: tool-registry-signature-decorator
explain: Demonstrates generating model-facing JSON Schemas from Python type hints and docstrings while preserving signatures through functools.wraps. Distinguishes returned tool errors (is_error: True) that allow model self-correction from fatal unhandled infrastructure exceptions that must halt execution, combining deterministic tool validation with flexible model reasoning.
steps: Decorate Python functions with metadata preservation and auto-generate strict JSON Schemas. || Dispatch tools with deterministic argument and boundary validation. || Return recoverable domain errors as tool observations while re-raising fatal infrastructure crashes.
expect: Tool registry schema generation, signature preservation, and error taxonomy verified successfully.

name: session-state-compaction-store
explain: Demonstrates partitioning agent memory into transient session scratchpads, durable conversation logs, and authoritative domain database records. Implements sliding-window turn compaction to summarize older turns when context grows, and enforces optimistic concurrency control (version locking) to prevent split-brain cross-replica race conditions.
steps: Partition active session state from durable conversation and transactional database records. || Compact older conversation turns into structured summaries when turn limits are reached. || Enforce optimistic concurrency locks on session updates to reject stale concurrent writes across server replicas.
expect: Session memory partitioning, compaction, and cross-replica continuity verified successfully.

name: provider-adapter-handshake
explain: Demonstrates what a unified provider adapter (like LiteLLM) abstracts versus what remains provider-specific. Standardizes chat messages, tool definitions, and response parsing across OpenAI and Anthropic, while isolating provider-specific parameters like extended thinking budgets and reasoning effort flags.
steps: Translate unified chat messages and tool definitions into OpenAI wire format with reasoning_effort. || Translate unified chat messages into Anthropic wire format with thinking.budget_tokens. || Normalize heterogeneous provider responses into a uniform typed output structure.
expect: Provider adapter abstraction and provider-specific parameter isolation verified successfully.

name: human-handoff-protocol
explain: Demonstrates why a human handoff requires an explicit state machine and protocol rather than a naive prompt instruction. Transitions the session from AUTONOMOUS to PAUSED_FOR_HUMAN, creates a structured support ticket with sentiment flags and pending actions, and silences the autonomous agent until a human supervisor resolves the case.
steps: Detect handoff triggers (user demand or low confidence) during conversation. || Transition session state to PAUSED_FOR_HUMAN and dispatch a structured support ticket to the queue. || Enforce gateway guardrails to block rogue autonomous agent output while awaiting human resolution.
expect: Human handoff protocol and state machine invariants verified successfully.

name: sdk-benchmark-reproducibility
explain: Demonstrates reproducible benchmarking for agent SDK applications using deterministic offline mock adapters. Compares candidate agent definitions against baselines across paired test suites, measuring genuine behavioral improvements (task success %, tool error elimination, and token efficiency) rather than superficial script pass rates.
steps: Configure deterministic mock adapters with fixed random seeds for offline testing. || Execute paired benchmark test suites comparing baseline and candidate agent trajectories. || Measure and verify statistically significant improvements in completion rate, error reduction, and token cost.
expect: Deterministic benchmark suite and genuine behavioral improvement verified successfully.
